job.text: Ah, yes!" said Bruin. "But you see this bird has no hands, though he has very ugly claws; so that doesn't help-- Well!" he cried, breaking off short, and once more addressing the hawk. "I don't see anything for it _but_ to wring your neck, do you? After all, it will keep you from being hungry again." But here the soft voice of the wood-pigeon interposed. "No, no! Bruin, dear," cried the gentle bird. "Give him something to eat, and let him go. If he had eaten nothing for a week
